sources.entry: ungoogled-chromium - A lightweight approach to removing Google web service dependency. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ungoogled-software/ungoogled-chromium) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A Chromium fork that strips out Google web service dependencies and background requests while staying close to the stock Chromium experience.
summary.what_it_does: This repository holds the common, cross-platform code for ungoogled-chromium, a drop-in replacement for Google Chromium. It removes functionality tied to Google domains (such as Google Cloud Messaging, Google Host Detector, and Safe Browsing) and removes pre-built binaries from the source via binary pruning. Domain substitution replaces many Google domains with non-existent ".qjz9zk" alternatives, and the browser is modified to block requests to them as a runtime fail-safe. It also adds opt-in privacy and control options, such as extra chrome://flags and command-line switches (disabled by default), a Suggestions URL field in the search engine editor, forcing pop-ups into tabs, and a "No Search" omnibox provider. The README states that patches, configuration flags, and custom scripts implement these changes, and that platform-specific repos hold the remaining build scripts. Pre-built packages are listed for many Linux distributions, macOS (Homebrew), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, Flatpak, Guix, and NixOS.
use_cases: Browse the web with Chromium without Google background services
Install a privacy-focused Chromium build on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD or OpenBSD
Build Chromium from source without Google web service dependencies
Disable Safe Browsing and other Google-specific Chromium features
Customize search engine suggestions in Chromium
Apply ungoogling patches to my own Chromium build
how_to_run: Platform-specific build repos are linked from the README's Source Code section
Use tags in the format {chromium_version}-{revision} to include the code in your own build
notable: Domain substitution replaces Google domains with non-existent '.qjz9zk' addresses and blocks connections to them as a fail-safe
Binary pruning removes pre-made binaries from the Chromium source
Most privacy features are off by default and must be enabled manually
Borrows features from Inox, Bromite, Debian, and Iridium Browser
Packaged for many Linux distributions plus macOS, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD
caveats: Safe Browsing is disabled, a deliberate trade-off that the README explains in the FAQ
Captive portal detection is broken by disabling the intranet redirect detector, though captive portals still work
Contributor binaries are not reproducible, so their authenticity cannot be guaranteed
This repo holds only common code; most users need a platform-specific repo and build steps
